failure_summary.description: Plans searched again, used unlisted cache keys, repeated completed work, or missed a newly requested domain instead of applying the latest turn to compatible cached results.
Search or refinement results were not consistently assigned to variables and saved to cache.
Flight time constraints were omitted or re-sent in a format the tool rejected, rather than correctly representing a deadline or reusing a cached time constraint.
The agent imported a cache module instead of calling the runtime-provided tools directly.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly covers incremental cache use, conversation-wide planning, and saving result objects, so repeating those rules is unlikely to help. Add only the missing flight-time deadline guidance and a direct-runtime-tools rule to prevent the observed time-window and import failures.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - For flight time constraints, map “arrive by T” or “no later than T” to an `arrival_time` range ending at T, using the earliest valid time-of-day endpoint and the time format accepted by the tool. Apply departure-time constraints to `departure_time`, not `arrival_time`. If a compatible cached result already covers a time constraint, do not resend it or search again merely to reapply it; refine only for newly introduced criteria.

## Runtime tool usage
- Travel tools and cache helpers are provided as runtime bindings. Call them directly; do not import, wrap, or redefine them. In particular, use the provided `get_results_from_cache` and `save_to_cache` functions rather than importing a cache module.
